stories.primary_headline: "Not applied its mind..." Gauhati High Court quashes Pranab Doley's detention order under NSA

primary_source.headline: "Not applied its mind..." Gauhati High Court quashes Pranab Doley's detention order under NSA
primary_source.content: Guwahati: More than 100 days after Pranab Doley, an indigenous rights activist in Assam, was detained under the National Security Act (NSA), Gauhati High Court on Friday quashed the order of his detention on the ground that the same was legally unsustainable.While quashing the detention order, the court observed that the detaining authority did not apply its mind as to whether or not the ordinary laws of the country was insufficient to deal with the activities of the petitioner.The bench of justice Kalyan Rai Surana and Justice Susmita Phukan Khaund had reserved its judgment on October 14. The 34-page judgment was pronounced on Friday.'He just raised voice for people, did nothing anti-national': Father of NSA detenue Pranab Doley Doley, who allegedly led indigenous farmers near Kaziranga National Park for a protest against construction of a five-star hotel allegeldly without properly compensating them, was arrested on July 13. He was, however, granted bail on July 29 but was detained under the NSA a day later. In the detention order, the state home department claimed that Doley was booked in several criminal cases in the past and his prevention detention was necessary in view of possibility of him continue to indulge in "activities prejudicial to maintenance of law and order." The court set aside the detention order on the grounds that Doley, 40, was detained on the strength of "stale cases," including those in which he had been discharged and acquitted. The court said out of the 13 cases, Doley had been acquitted in nine while legal process was underway in the rest. The bench said although the detaining authority alleged Doley's involvement in road blockades and damages to public properties, no particulars of the alleged offence, including place, dateand time of commission of such alleged offences have been disclosed. "Thus, the allegations against the petitioner is vague and bereft of material particulars..."The court said relevant facts and grounds of his detention and relevant documents were not furnished to Doley, disallowing him to make an effective representation before the prescribed authorities. The authorities also did not act on his representation against his detention, the court said. Foreign trips: The HC said although the home department claimed that Doley had visited foreign countries 14 times, it did not give the details of anti-India activity by the petitioner. "The grounds of detention also does not specify in which foreign visit the petitioner made any speech or statement which has brought disrepute to the country or has encouraged seditious activity against the country. There is no information as to where the petitioner gave any speech or statement, which had the potential to threaten the security or integrity of the country, territorial, moral, political, social, or otherwise."The bench said Doley's repetitive foreign visits, by itself, is not an act which would warrant preventive detention of a person and curtail his fundamental right to visit a country of his choice. "....except for a vagu allegation regarding foreign visits and suspicious foreign exchange receipts, the detaining authority has not furnished to the petitioner any materials showing how his foreign visits and receipt of foreign exchange amounts to activities that is prejudicial to the interest of the State, its security and integrity, or has affected public order," the court said.Three lawyers, Santanu Borthakur, Dipesh Kumar Agarwala and S. Dey appeared on behalf of Doley. Timeline of eventsDoley, who did Master in Social Work from TISS, Mumbai, was arrested on July 13 following a protest against construciton of a 5-star hotel near Kaziranga National Park without allegedly compensating the indigenous farmers.He was granted bail on July 29.He was detained under the NSA on July 30.State home department claimed that Doley's prevention detention was necessary in view of possibility of him continue to indulge in "activities prejudicial to maintenance of law and order." His father Lakhi Doley had said Pranab was detained for raising voice for the indigenous farmers.

stories.primary_headline: Crackerless Diwali must be people’s movement, not a court order: Supreme Court

primary_source.headline: Crackerless Diwali must be people’s movement, not a court order: Supreme Court
primary_source.content: New Delhi: The Supreme Court on Friday said a crackerless Diwali should be a people’s movement, not a judicial initiative, as it slammed the commercialisation of festivals and observed that restrictions alone cannot curb Delhi’s pollution crisis. “No restriction is going to work. The more orders we pass, the more violations will multiply,” a bench led by Chief Justice of India Surya Kant remarked while hearing the suo motu case on air pollution in Delhi-NCR.Anti-pollution measures doomed unless authorities enforce directions on ground: Supreme Court  “We keep talking, make statements but point is AQI is already touching 400,” the CJI remarked, while urging the Centre and states to educate farmers on the economics of stubble burning. The court said only a people’s movement for a crackerless Diwali and responsible celebration can save Delhi.&nbsp; The city-wide Air Quality Index stood around 389 to 391 in the ‘very poor’ category, with several areas slipping towards ‘severe’, according to the Central Pollution Control Board. Justice Joymalya Bagchi, also on the bench, said commercialisation of festivals was a major problem.&nbsp; The CJI agreed, noting that the rich had turned Diwali gift exchange into a social and status symbol, fuelling waste and pollution. “Why don’t we revert to our original customs,” the CJI asked, stressing that celebrations must be accompanied by responsibility towards the environment. Diwali was meant to be a festival of lights, not a festival of smoke, he said. The court flagged bumper-to-bumper traffic in Delhi-NCR and questioned authorities on anti-pollution measures. It made clear that the poor should not be blamed for the crisis.&nbsp; “Poor people do not generate any pollution. They are the sufferers. It is those who can afford it and those who can contribute to it,” the CJI remarked.&nbsp; He also noted that Diwali is an important livelihood period for those dependent on seasonal work and that this aspect should be considered. The Centre’s counsel attributed the rise in pollution to the festive season and movement of people.&nbsp;Protests can't choke livelihoods: Supreme Court on demonstrations in Delhi's Ramlila Maidan ahead of festive period  The bench said it would go by expert opinion on closing physical classes in schools if the AQI rises further. It urged governments to educate farmers, observing that they would stop burning stubble once they understood the economics. A crackerless Diwali cannot be imposed and must be embraced by the people, the court said.

stories.primary_headline: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM

primary_source.headline: Firms should publish salaries in job adverts ahead of new law, says PM
primary_source.content: Andy Burnham says it isn't fair if an employer 'holds all the cards' The government is planning to make pay details compulsory in adverts, with legislation on the issue being brought forward "as soon as possible". It argues the change will help jobseekers, particularly those applying for their first job, and could help prevent pay discrimination. However, one industry group said setting pay was a complex process and regulating adverts was not always suitable. Burnham said the current system felt "weighted against the applicant" and the changes were aimed at "tilting the scales back". "It can be quite soul destroying for young people these days, applying for jobs when the salary is not listed but sometimes they're not getting a reply," he told the BBC. The prime minister added that publishing salaries in adverts was also important for closing the gender pay gap.

stories.primary_headline: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw urges social media platforms to take greater responsibility for online harms

primary_source.headline: IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw urges social media platforms to take greater responsibility for online harms
primary_source.content: New Delhi: Social media platforms must assume greater responsibility for the content they host, take necessary steps to ensure child safety, ensure algorithmic transparency, and provide citizens with an effective mechanism to address grievances, Union IT Minister Ashwini Vaishnaw said on Friday.Speaking on the evolving nature of the internet and social media landscape, Vaishnaw asserted that platforms can no longer remain passive. They must proactively protect society from serious online harms, including “digital arrest” scams, he said. Kolkata teen blindfolded, set ablaze; police arrest 3, assault allegedly filmed for social media reel “Today, social media platforms must take the responsibility for child safety, for women’s safety, for digital arrest, for the harms which come to the citizens… social media platforms must take proactive steps. Unlike the past, they must take proactive steps to make sure that our society is safe,” said Vaishnaw, who also holds the Information and Broadcasting portfolio.The minister stressed the need to give ordinary citizens a stronger voice on these platforms. Currently, he noted, when content causes serious harm, the only options available are approaching the courts or the police. He called for a robust and effective grievance redressal system that allows people to seek remedies directly.“If something is there on the social media platforms which causes serious harm to the citizens, the citizens have only the recourse to go to the courts or go to the police. There has to be a good, very effective mechanism by which the citizens get voice to address their grievances,” Vaishnaw said.
